correctness.rationale: The proof uses the probability-normalized Bergman monomials, exact incomplete-beta recurrence and analytic-shift weights, not a numerical interpolation. Gamma-ratio asymptotics and separate near-zero and tail controls prove weak convergence and the three Schatten regimes. Maximal modes are handled separately at \(\beta<1\), \(\beta=1\) and \(\beta>1\); the \(\beta=1\) comparison is an exact successive-ratio inequality. Direct independent finite matrix and beta-function checks in checker.py passed. All \(p>0\) and \(\beta>0\) with parameters fixed are quantified; no finite experiment is treated as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A geometrically canonical increasing disk cutoff approaches the identity strongly, yet its noncommutation with coordinate multiplication transports exactly one unit of trace-class mass toward monomial degrees of order \(1/\varepsilon\). The limiting gamma law explains the full sharp Schatten p transition, including a critical logarithmic singularity at \(\alpha=-1/p\) for \(p>1\), and a nontrivial square-root mode scale at \(\alpha=0\). These distinguish trace, operator and quasi-Schatten topologies and supply reproducible constants for all weights and exponents, rather than an arbitrary special-function exercise. The theorem neither requires nor claims downstream applications.
